documents.title: Stool test
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your FIT stool test is negative. We'll repeat it every year as your colon cancer screening. Thanks for getting it done.

documents.title: Big news
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Well. Took two home tests this morning, both positive. Last period started March 10. Completely unplanned and I'm honestly still sitting on the bathroom floor. I'm 45, is this even safe? What do I do first? I'm still taking the prenatal vitamin, I never stopped.

documents.title: RE: Big news
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Aisha, that is a lot to take in before 8 am. Plenty of women your age have healthy pregnancies, and you have done this four times before; it does mean you'll get closer monitoring, which is a good thing. By your dates you're about 5 weeks. Keep taking the prenatal vitamin. I'm sending a referral to obstetrics today so you can get in for a first visit and dating ultrasound in the next few weeks. Call or text me if you have bleeding or bad cramping, and grab time with me if you want to talk any of it through.

documents.title: RE: RE: Big news
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you. Breathing again.

documents.title: Referral sent
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: OB referral faxed with last office note and med list. Called pt to let her know; OB scheduling will reach out for an 8-10 week new OB appointment.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, patient at home in her office, identity verified.

About 10 weeks. Had her first OB visit last week, dating scan matched her period. Nausea manageable. She asked for this visit because the worry has been loud: about her age, about the baby, about the logistics with four kids. GAD-7 10, PHQ-9 4. Sleeping 6 hours. No panic attacks. No thoughts of self-harm.

She was offered first-trimester screening at OB and turned it down for now. She said she didn't want a number to obsess over yet. Her choice; told her she can always ask OB about what's still available later.

Meds: prenatal vitamin. NKDA.

A/P: GAD, more active in early pregnancy. Moderate range. Discussed options including counseling and, if needed, medication that is reasonable in pregnancy; she wants to keep going without meds for now and lean on her husband. Will check in at least once more this pregnancy. She knows to text.

reports.text: Single live intrauterine pregnancy, cephalic. Fetal heart rate normal. Biometry consistent with 17 weeks 0 days by LMP. Nuchal fold thickened. Nasal bone hypoplastic. Femur length short for gestational age. Four-chamber view suspicious for an endocardial cushion defect; not well seen at this gestation. Placenta posterior, clear of the cervix. Amniotic fluid normal. Known intramural fibroids noted, not encroaching on the placenta or lower segment. Cervix closed.
reports.conclusion: Second-trimester soft markers (thickened nuchal fold, hypoplastic nasal bone, short femur) and a possible endocardial cushion defect. Findings raise concern for fetal aneuploidy. Genetic counseling recommended.

documents.title: Prenatal Visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Outside obstetrics group
Visit: 07/07/2025
Patient: Aisha Pierre, 45, G6P4014 at 17w0d by LMP (EDD 12/15/2025)
cc: primary care

Returning for routine prenatal care. She has stress urinary incontinence and a fibroid uterus, both evaluated by our department in 2022. This pregnancy was conceived spontaneously and has been uncomplicated to date. No bleeding, no abdominal pain, feels well.

Today she is worried about a chromosomal condition given her age. She declined first-trimester screening earlier and now wants whatever testing is still open to her.

Meds: prenatal vitamin. Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother with fibroids; no known chromosomal or genetic disorders, no Down syndrome in the family.
Social: no tobacco, no alcohol.

Exam: well appearing. Fetal heart tones present by Doppler. Fundus measuring at dates.

Ultrasound today (see report): thickened nuchal fold, hypoplastic nasal bone, short femur, and a possible endocardial cushion defect.

Assessment/plan:
- Advanced maternal age with ultrasound markers concerning for aneuploidy, trisomy 21 being the leading concern. We spent a long time on what the findings can and cannot tell us. She opted for second-trimester maternal serum (quad) screening, drawn today; this also gives a neural tube defect risk.
- Referral to maternal-fetal medicine and genetic counseling to discuss diagnostic testing.
- Next visit in about 3-4 weeks.

Allergies: NKDA.

Obstetrics

documents.title: Maternal serum quad screen
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Second-trimester maternal serum screen (AFP, hCG, uE3, inhibin A)
Collected 07/07/2025, reported 07/11/2025
Gestational age at collection: 17w0d by LMP
Maternal age at EDD: 46

Trisomy 21: SCREEN POSITIVE, risk 1 in 12
Trisomy 18: screen negative
Open neural tube defect: screen negative, risk not increased

Comment: Diagnostic testing offered. Patient informed by phone 07/11; genetic counseling and MFM consultation already scheduled.

Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Screening result
documents.author: patient
documents.body: OB called Friday. The screen came back high risk for Down syndrome, 1 in 12. I have the genetic counselor and the amnio on Wednesday. Just wanted you to know. I'm OK, ish.

documents.title: RE: Screening result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for telling me. I'm sorry you are carrying this over a weekend. The amnio will give you a real answer instead of a probability. I'm here after Wednesday or before, text anytime, and I'll open a video slot for you whenever you want one.

documents.title: Maternal-Fetal Medicine Consultation
documents.author: maternal-fetal medicine
documents.body:
Outside maternal-fetal medicine
Date: 07/16/2025
Patient: Aisha Pierre, 45, G6P4014, 18w2d

Reason: genetic counseling and diagnostic testing after a screen-positive quad screen (trisomy 21 risk 1 in 12) and second-trimester ultrasound markers.

Counseling: met with our genetic counselor with her husband present. Reviewed the screen, the markers, the difference between screening and diagnosis, and the options of amniocentesis, cell-free DNA, or no further testing. Family pedigree reviewed: four healthy children, one first-trimester loss; no known chromosomal or genetic conditions on either side. She chose amniocentesis.

Procedure: transabdominal amniocentesis under continuous ultrasound guidance, spinal needle through a fundal window away from the placenta and fibroids, single pass. Clear amniotic fluid sent for rapid FISH and karyotype. Fetal heart activity normal afterward. She tolerated it well.

Plan: FISH in 1-2 days, karyotype in 7-10 days. Pelvic rest 24 hours, call for fluid leakage, bleeding or fever.

Medications: prenatal vitamin. Allergies: NKDA.

Maternal-Fetal Medicine

documents.title: Prenatal cytogenetics report
documents.author: genetics laboratory
documents.body:
Specimen: amniotic fluid, collected 07/16/2025

Interphase FISH (13, 18, 21, X, Y), reported 07/18/2025: signal pattern consistent with three copies of chromosome 21. Results for 13, 18 and the sex chromosomes are normal.

Chromosome analysis (G-banding), reported 07/25/2025: 47 chromosomes in all cells examined, with an additional chromosome 21. Full (non-mosaic) trisomy 21.

Interpretation: abnormal. Consistent with Down syndrome. Genetic counseling is recommended and has been arranged by the referring provider.

documents.title: Thinking of you
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Aisha, the amniocentesis report reached me yesterday. I know OB will go through it with you Thursday. I'm thinking of you, and I'm here for whatever you need afterward.

conditions.label: Maternal care for chromosomal abnormality in fetus, trisomy 21

documents.title: Prenatal Visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Outside obstetrics group
Visit: 07/31/2025
Patient: Aisha Pierre, 45, G6P4014 at 20w3d
cc: primary care

Here for routine surveillance and to go over results. History of stress incontinence, fibroid uterus and generalized anxiety. Physically the pregnancy is going smoothly.

Results reviewed together: quad screen positive for trisomy 21 (1 in 12); amniocentesis FISH and karyotype show full trisomy 21. The second-trimester ultrasound markers seen on 07/07 (thickened nuchal fold, hypoplastic nasal bone, short femur, possible endocardial cushion defect) fit with this.

She and her husband have had time with the genetic counselor and with MFM. She has decided to continue the pregnancy. She was tearful but clear. We talked about what the rest of the pregnancy will look like: growth scans, a fetal echocardiogram to look more closely at the heart, and delivery planning with pediatrics.

Meds: prenatal vitamin. Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BP normal, fetal heart tones present, fundal height appropriate.

Plan:
- Fetal trisomy 21, confirmed. Pregnancy continuing.
- Fetal echocardiogram scheduled.
- Offered social work and a Down syndrome parent support contact; she took the information.
- Return in 4 weeks.

Allergies: NKDA.

Obstetrics

documents.title: Results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: It's confirmed, the baby has Down syndrome. We're keeping the pregnancy, that was never really a question for us, but my brain won't turn off. Can I get on your schedule next week? Video is fine.

documents.title: RE: Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Of course. I have Wednesday at 12:30 open for video and put you in it. Until then, if a night gets bad, text me.

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, pt at home, identity confirmed.

21 weeks. Amnio confirmed trisomy 21 last week; she and her husband are continuing the pregnancy. She is lying awake reading about heart defects and early intervention, feels on edge most days, irritable with the kids. Eating OK. Working, but slower. GAD-7 13, PHQ-9 6. Denies thoughts of harming herself. No panic attacks.

She has the fetal echo on 8/20. OB connected her with a parent support group.

A/P: GAD, worsened with a stressful prenatal diagnosis. Moderate. Talked about counseling vs medication. She wants to start with a therapist who works with pregnant patients and hold off on medication, will reconsider if it isn't enough. Referral placed to a perinatal counselor. Check back in about a month, sooner if needed.

documents.title: Fetal Echocardiogram
documents.author: pediatric cardiology
documents.body:
Outside fetal cardiology program
Study date: 08/20/2025
Mother: Aisha Pierre, 45, 23w2d
Indication: fetal trisomy 21; possible endocardial cushion defect on the 17-week obstetric scan.

Findings: situs solitus, levocardia. Normal four-chamber view with normal atrial and ventricular septa. Two separate atrioventricular valves with normal offset and no regurgitation. Normal outflow tracts with normal great artery relationship. Normal aortic arch. Ductal arch normal. Regular rhythm, normal rate. No pericardial effusion.

Impression: structurally normal fetal heart. No atrioventricular septal defect seen; the possible endocardial cushion defect on the earlier scan is not confirmed.

Recommendation: routine newborn echocardiogram after delivery, as for all infants with trisomy 21. No further fetal cardiac imaging needed.

Maternal allergies: NKDA.

Pediatric Cardiology

documents.title: Prenatal Visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Outside obstetrics group
Visit: 10/24/2025
Patient: Aisha Pierre, 45, G6P4014 at 32w4d, fetal trisomy 21 (structurally normal heart on fetal echo)
cc: primary care

Came in for her scheduled visit and reported that the baby has been moving less over the past day. Otherwise the pregnancy has been followed closely here without other problems.

Meds: prenatal vitamin. Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BP 120/78, HR 82. Fetal heart rate 140.

Ultrasound: AFI 3 cm.
NST: baseline 140, minimal variability, no accelerations, no decelerations.

Assessment: oligohydramnios at 32 weeks with decreased fetal movement and a nonreactive NST.

Plan: sent directly to labor and delivery triage for extended monitoring. Per the triage note, the tracing became reactive with accelerations and moderate variability after about an hour, no contractions, no decelerations, membranes intact. Discharged home with twice-weekly NSTs and amniotic fluid checks, daily kick counts, and strict return precautions. Delivery timing will be planned around 36-37 weeks if the fluid stays low.

Allergies: NKDA.

Obstetrics

documents.title: FYI
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Spent the afternoon on the monitor at the hospital, low fluid. They sent me home. I'll be there twice a week now. Not sleeping tonight.

documents.title: RE: FYI
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: I saw the note come through. Twice-weekly checks are exactly the right safety net, and the tracing looked good before they let you go. Text me if you need to vent between visits.

documents.title: Obstetric Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Regional hospital, labor and delivery
Admitted: 11/21/2025  Discharged: 11/24/2025
Patient: Aisha Pierre, 46 (birthday on the day of admission), G6 now P4115

Admission diagnosis: oligohydramnios at 36w4d with continued decreased fetal movement. Known fetal trisomy 21 with a structurally normal heart on fetal echocardiogram.

Hospital course: Seen from her twice-weekly testing for persistently reduced movement. BP 122/78, HR 88. Fetal heart rate 140. Ultrasound AFI 4 cm, confirming ongoing low fluid. Admitted for continuous fetal monitoring. Given oligohydramnios at 36 weeks, plan made for delivery; induction started that evening with oxytocin, followed by artificial rupture of membranes. Labor progressed normally. Spontaneous vaginal delivery 11/22/2025 of a liveborn infant at 36w5d. Intact perineum, no laceration. Placenta delivered spontaneously and complete; bleeding within normal limits. The infant was examined by pediatrics; features consistent with trisomy 21, as known prenatally. Newborn care, including the newborn echocardiogram, per the pediatric team.

Postpartum course uneventful. Afebrile, vitals stable, ambulating, voiding, pain controlled with ibuprofen.

Discharge diagnoses: vaginal delivery at 36w5d; oligohydramnios; fetal trisomy 21.

Discharge medications:
- Ibuprofen 600 mg every 6 hours as needed for pain
- Prenatal vitamin daily

Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: obstetrics postpartum visit in 6 weeks; primary care within 1-2 weeks. Call for heavy bleeding, fever, severe headache or low mood.

Obstetrics

documents.title: Baby's here
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Delivered yesterday morning! Induced Friday night for the low fluid. Everyone is OK. Peds is looking after the baby. Going home tomorrow probably.

documents.title: RE: Baby's here
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations to all of you. Rest. Our nurse will call after you're home and we'll see you in the next week or two.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt 2 days after discharge from L&D. Vaginal delivery 11/22, home 11/24. She feels sore but OK, bleeding lighter each day, no fever, no headache. Taking ibuprofen a few times a day and the prenatal vitamin. Baby is home with her and following with pediatrics. Mood: "tired and emotional, but OK." Visit booked with PCP 12/3 at 10:20.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-discharge visit, 11 days after vaginal delivery.

Hospital course reviewed from the discharge summary: admitted 11/21 at 36w4d for continued decreased movement with AFI 4 cm, induced with oxytocin, delivered vaginally 11/22 at 36w5d, no laceration, home 11/24. Baby has trisomy 21 as expected, and is followed by pediatrics.

Now: lochia light, no fever, pain minimal, using ibuprofen once a day at most. Leaking with coughing about the same as before the pregnancy. Sleeping in pieces. Mood is up and down; she's teary sometimes but enjoying the baby, still seeing her counselor every other week. GAD-7 12, PHQ-9 5. No thoughts of harming herself or the baby. Husband home for another two weeks.

Meds: prenatal vitamin; ibuprofen prn. NKDA.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet, BP normal. Weight up from her pre-pregnancy baseline as expected. Looks tired, smiling. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, fundus nontender below the umbilicus. Calves soft, no swelling.

A/P
1. S/p vaginal delivery, recovering well. Postpartum visit with OB in early January.
2. GAD, still moderate, and the early weeks are a high-risk time. Counseling continues. Reviewed warning signs of postpartum depression; she and her husband know to call. Will see her again by video in about two months.
3. Mammogram order for the spring.
4. Ibuprofen as needed, short term.

Outside obstetrics group
Visit: 01/05/2026
Patient: Aisha Pierre, 46, 6 weeks after vaginal delivery at 36w5d
cc: primary care

Feels well physically. Bleeding stopped at 4 weeks. No pain. Infant doing well with pediatrics.

Exam: BP normal. Breasts without masses. Abdomen soft, uterus involuting, irregular contour from known fibroids. Perineum healed. No tenderness.

Assessment: routine postpartum course, uncomplicated.
Plan: resume normal activity and pelvic floor exercises. Routine gynecologic follow-up.

Meds: prenatal vitamin. Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 6.5 months postpartum. Anxiety is the best it's been in a year, GAD-7 8. Counseling down to monthly. Baby is doing well.
The leakage with coughing and exercise is the same as before this pregnancy, not worse, but she's done living with it and wants to go back to urogynecology to talk about what else can be done. Still doing the exercises some days. No dysuria, no blood.
Meds: prenatal vitamin. Done with ibuprofen. NKDA.

O: vitals per flowsheet, weight trending down toward baseline. Well appearing. Abdomen soft, nontender. Mood good, affect full.

A/P
1. Stress urinary incontinence, persistent. Re-referral to urogynecology placed.
2. GAD, improved. Continue counseling. No medication.
3. Annual physical in October with labs.
